sources.entry: What Team Structure is Right for DevOps to Flourish?

summary.name: DevOps Topologies
summary.one_liner: A essay-style catalogue of DevOps team structures, describing bad "anti-types" and good "topologies" for organising Dev and Ops collaboration.
keywords: infrastructure as a service ops team
use_cases: Assessing which DevOps team structure suits an organisation
Spotting common DevOps anti-patterns in a company
Deciding whether to create a temporary DevOps team
Planning a move from siloed Dev and Ops to shared responsibility
Understanding when an SRE team model fits
Explaining DevOps org design to a team
summary.what_it_does: The page describes nine or so DevOps team topologies and eight anti-types, each with a short explanation of how it works and where it fits. It covers patterns such as Dev and Ops collaboration, Ops as an infrastructure platform, DevOps as an external service, temporary DevOps teams, an advocacy team, the Google-style SRE hand-off model, container-driven collaboration, and Dev and DBA collaboration. It states that no single structure suits every organisation and that the choice depends on product set, technical leadership, and Ops capability, drawing on Conway's Law. Some entries include suitability and potential effectiveness ratings (HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW).
notable: Catalogues anti-types (bad patterns) alongside good topologies, with suitability notes for each
Based on Conway's Law and the idea that DevOps should serve value delivery rather than cost or automation alone
Links to the author's Team Topologies book and CC BY-SA A1 posters summarising the material
caveats: The page promotes a paid book and paid posters; the essay itself is presented as a reference guide, not a definitive model
Several topologies are described as having potential effectiveness that depends heavily on organisational maturity
